nodes.question: What does the OECD report "Accelerating Climate Action Refocusing Policies through a Well-Being Lens" focus on?
nodes.answer: The OECD report focuses on accelerating climate action by refocusing policies through a well-being lens, highlighting the importance of considering well-being in climate policy decisions.

nodes.question: How do non-state actors contribute to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) process?
nodes.answer: Non-state actors contribute informally by sharing expertise, overseeing the progress of Parties, and supporting ambition through hybrid multilateral governance, though they do not directly participate in decision-making for negotiation texts.
nodes.paragraph: The multilateralism of the UNFCCC process relies on procedural justice8, ensuring stakeholders equitable access to decision-making processes 9 through justice norms such as participation, transpar - ency, accuracy and correctability10. nodes.question: What does the proposed new framework aim to improve in carbon price forecasting?
nodes.answer: The new framework aims to provide a better-informed basis for investment decisions and climate governance in China and the EU.
nodes.paragraph: While so far there has been an abundance of studies to explore carbon price forecasting, it is currently dif cultto guarantee that any single algorithm proposed in the literature will consistently outperformothers all the time. The optimal prediction model may change as the data sample varies.A two-step technique is widely used in the existing literature, speci cally, the process ofdecomposition followed by a single learning method, in an effort to more accurately predictthe price outcome of a given set of data. However, the data distribution characteristics ofthe different sub-series are distinct and so the prediction results may not always be optimalwhen using the same approach. This paper therefore proposes a new two-step frameworkfor predicting international carbon prices which can serve as a reference for better-informedinvestment decisions and climate governance in both China and the EU. More precisely, we rst decompose the carbon prices into factors based on trend and period, using the Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) approach. The second stage is then to nd the best-performing model from among the numerous available prediction models for 123 Annals of Operations Research (2025) 345:1267 1295 1269 the factors of trend and period.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Global climate governance_qna_004
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What country within the EU is the focus of the paper regarding climate strategy?
nodes.answer: The focus of the paper regarding climate strategy is on Spain.
nodes.paragraph: Notable among such actions is the EuropeanClimate Law, enacted in June 2021, which sets a legally binding target of net zero GHG emissions by 2050 and requires both Member States and EU institutions to take the necessary measures to meet this target. This Law also sets an intermediatetarget for 2030 of reducing GHG emissions in the EU as a whole by 55% (from 1990 levels). The success of these agreements critically hinges on the implementation of effective policies at the national level. In this paper, we focus on a particular countrywithin the EU, namely, Spain, in which the basic pillars of such a strategy are the Climate Change and Energy Transition Law, the National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) 2021 2030, the National Plan for Adapting to Climate Change (PNACC by its Spanish abbreviation) and the Just Transition Strategy; see Banco de Espa a (2021 ). For example, within the framework of the Law on Climate Change and Energy Transition, proposals have been made for notable changes to patterns of mobility and the creation of low-emission zones in major cities.
